root_idea.summary: The root centers on tearing, piercing, or making an opening in something.
root_idea.development: From physical rending or penetration, the lexical range extends to traversing land, passages through which wind moves, figurative fabrication without proper basis, confusion or lack of skill, and expansive generosity.

senses.definition: To make a hole in, perforate, pierce, bore, slit, or tear something.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive physical action; in the Quran it is used of making a hole in a ship.

senses.definition: To cut across or traverse the earth, or to pierce it through toward its far side.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression خَرْقُ الأَرْضِ, the usage is explained both as traversing the earth and as boring through it; the wording should not be reduced to a simple garment-tearing sense.

senses.definition: To fabricate or falsely attribute something; to forge a claim without knowledge.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the object is an invented attribution of sons and daughters to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wind, to pass along or blow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical usage describing the movement of wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a sheep, to have a round hole or perforation in its ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verb describing the condition of the animal's ear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain in a house or tent without leaving it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional intransitive construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a hunted gazelle or bird, to become so frightened that it cannot flee, rise, or fly, and clings to the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is specifically described for frightened game animals and birds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bewildered, perplexed, or unable to see the right course; to lose one's composure or intellect through fear, shame, anxiety, or distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom وَقَعَ فَخَرِقَ, the expression is reported to mean that someone fell down dead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be rough, ungentle, clumsy, awkward, unskilled, foolish, or deficient in understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of conduct, workmanship, handling affairs, or practical skill.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make holes in or tear something extensively, in several or many places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II gives an intensive sense relative to خَرَقَ; commonly used of cloth and similar things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lie or falsely attribute something repeatedly or emphatically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Quranic reading of 6:100 uses this intensified form, distinct from the QAC-attested Form I group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to become confounded or perplexed, so that he cannot see the right course or is deprived of reason.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become perforated, pierced, cut, slit, or torn in several or many places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive or middle construction, especially of garments and similar objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become wide or expanded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Form V usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a wide or ample range in liberality, bounty, or munificence; to be profuse in generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with في السخاء and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wind, to blow irregularly rather than in one uniform direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical usage applied to wind moving through a wide country.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass through, over, or across; to traverse land without following a road; or to enter through the midst of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same construction can describe making a mosque or house into a thoroughfare, entering among people, or wind passing through trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole or perforation; also a portion of something that has been pierced, slit, rent, or torn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of garments, walls, ears, and similar objects; plural خُرُوقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A far-extending desert or wide tract of land, especially one through which winds pass irregularly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun; plural خُرُوقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant resembling القُسْط and having leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Roughness, ungentleness, clumsiness, awkwardness, unskilfulness, foolishness, or ignorance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun opposed to رِفْقٌ; it can also denote deficient understanding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In نَوْمَةُ الخُرْقِ, the sleep taken during the forenoon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vulva of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage associated with expansiveness in generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young man excellent or distinguished in mind, manners, address, speech, appearance, or courage, especially with a generous disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal descriptor whose positive qualities include generosity and excellence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a spear, highly esteemed, prized, excellent, or rare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet for a valued spear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young gazelle or similar animal frightened while hunted and unable to rise or flee; likewise a frightened or impatient bird unable to fly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival noun describing immobilization from fright.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person confounded, perplexed, amazed, or deprived of reason through fear or shame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal adjective; see also the corresponding Form I and Form IV verbal usages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ashes, so called because they remain clinging to the ground after the people have departed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized noun usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or torn-off portion of a garment or cloth; a rag or patched garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression for a devotee's ragged garment is reported, with that particular application noted as probably postclassical; plural خِرَقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A portion of a swarm of locusts, smaller than a رِجْل.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective-unit usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A womb rent by a fetus and consequently unable to conceive afterward; also a she-camel with such a womb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical and animal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a well, having its side or lateral part broken from the water upward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the structure of a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shallow water channel that is not without trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where a valley expands as it comes to an end.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun describing a valley's widening terminus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed tract of land containing herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun; plural خُرُقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested geographical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A violent, cold, or irregular wind; in some reports, a wind that returns, blows for a long time, or even blows gently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve several descriptions, including contrasting ones; the term is applied to wind understood as penetrating or tearing through the air.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small bird that clings to the ground, identified variously as a bird smaller than a lark or as a kind of sparrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bird name; plural خَرَارِقُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sharp or cutting sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival epithet for a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An event that breaks through or infringes the usual course of nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for an extraordinary or miraculous event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Profound or penetrating in learning or science.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later usage explicitly marked as belonging to present-day language.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe, having a round perforation in its ear; of an ear, perforated or bored.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form خَرْقَاءُ is used for the ewe and the ear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, placing its toe on the ground before the sole of its foot; of a she-camel, failing to place the hind feet where the forefeet were placed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of camel gait, associated in the source with a generous quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough, ungentle, clumsy, awkward, unskilled, foolish, or ignorant man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of practical work, handicraft, management, or deficient understanding; feminine خَرْقَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard or difficult journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional descriptive expression, رِحْلَةٌ خَرْقَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone at the inner end of a watering trough, used as a standing place for drawing water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object associated with a watering trough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An orifice of the body, such as the mouth, nose, ear, or anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَخَارِقُ is more commonly reported than the singular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confounded or deprived of reason; by extension, silent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participial adjective of Form IV with a lexicalized extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a road, not causing a traveller to become confounded or lose the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed negative construction applied to a road.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A twisted kerchief, bundle of rags, inflated skin, or wooden sword used as a toy for striking in play.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is connected with the idea of rending the air; in a traditional expression, lightning is called the angels' instruments for driving the clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical or extended nominal usage distinct from the toy implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man handsome or well formed in body or appearance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival personal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who escapes or extricates himself from difficult situations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended personal descriptor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person skilled in managing affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal descriptor of practical resourcefulness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wild bull that traverses far-extending districts or escapes pursuing dogs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal name explained through the root's movement sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who engages actively in wars or fights.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized personal descriptor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person denied prosperity or good fortune, into whose hand wealth does not fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression مَخْرُوقُ الكَفِّ means one who gains or obtains nothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who goes around camels, urges them, and actively manages them with skill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized personal descriptor of camel management.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A passage or place of passing; by extension, a country or district wide or far-extending enough to traverse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial noun of Form VIII.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place through which winds pass or blow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional geographical construction, مُخْتَرَقُ الرِّيَاحِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having clothing rent or torn, especially through long travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective applied to a person or to clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick or swift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended adjectival usage.

cautions: The Quranic expression in 17:37 supports both the sense of traversing the earth and the interpretation of boring through it; these are retained within one Quran-attested constructional sense.
Lane reports an alternative Quranic reading with Form II خَرَّقُوا in 6:100, but the supplied QAC form group is Form I خَرَقُوا.

The Classical term خَرِيقٌ for wind is reported with several descriptions, including contrasting ones such as violent and gentle; this variation is preserved rather than forced into a single physical profile.
